Implementation Plan Implementation Plan — Issue #9809 (unblock-judge fix-up for #9733: send unblock and stall-recovery work to the issue's open implementation PR) Planning ref: `orchestrator/project-9650` @ `1e9e0456b07b00592160b82190a63d9f1bc5eab6` (Integration branch mismatch: false). ## Automation / wiring summary (§20.E) - **New or existing code:** this only changes existing code. It extends `scripts/unblock_actions.py`, `scripts/unblock_judge.sh` and `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`. There are no new scripts, no supervisor, no DB work and no entry in `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md`. - **Entry points (unchanged triggers):** - `.github/workflows/unblock_judge.yml` (its existing schedule and dispatch) runs `scripts/unblock_judge.sh`. - `.github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml` (the poller's existing schedule) runs `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` stall recovery. - Both workflows get one env pass-through line, `UNBLOCK_EXISTING_PR_ROUTING_ENABLED: ${{ vars.UNBLOCK_EXISTING_PR_ROUTING_ENABLED || 'true' }}`. This follows the existing `UNBLOCK_JUDGE_WAIT_ENABLED` / `ENABLE_STALL_MERGED_PR_GUARD` lines. - Every script also defaults the flag itself (§8). The PR-head copy of a helper staged under `main`'s YAML therefore behaves the same. ## Files likely to change - `scripts/unblock_actions.py` - `scripts/unblock_judge.sh` - `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` - `.github/workflows/unblock_judge.yml` - `.github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml` - `tests/test_unblock_judge.py` - `tests/test_stall_existing_impl_pr_routing.py` (new) - `README.md` - `changelog.d/9809-unblock-existing-pr-routing.md` (new) - `agents.d/9809-unblock-existing-pr-routing.md` (new) ## Acceptance ACCEPTANCE: test tests/test_unblock_judge.py::test_issue_reset_routes_to_open_implementation_pr red-on-base ACCEPTANCE: test tests/test_unblock_judge.py::test_existing_pr_routing_flag_off_keeps_approve ACCEPTANCE: test tests/test_unblock_judge.py::test_issue_reset_without_implementation_pr_keeps_approve ACCEPTANCE: test tests/test_unblock_judge.py::test_impl_pr_subcommand_selects_only_trusted_implementation_pr red-on-base ACCEPTANCE: test tests/test_stall_existing_impl_pr_routing.py red-on-base ACCEPTANCE: post-merge none: harness-only change that takes effect on the next scheduled unblock-judge and poller runs; no post-merge workflow checks it ## Functions or modules to implement ### 1. `scripts/unblock_actions.py` **Flag reader.** Add `_existing_pr_routing_enabled(env=None) -> bool`, copying the shape of `_target_repo_guard_enabled` (around L591). - Reads `UNBLOCK_EXISTING_PR_ROUTING_ENABLED`. - Unset, empty or `true` in any case returns on. - `false` returns off. - Any other value returns off and prints `warning: UNBLOCK_EXISTING_PR_ROUTING_ENABLED is not true or false; existing-PR routing is off` to stderr. **New constant.** `EXISTING_PR_ROUTED_STOPS = ("needs-human", "blocked", "implement-diagnose-failed") + GUARD_STOPS`. `GUARD_STOPS` is at L173. **`_context()` (L403–512).** Add a new output key `"implementation_pr"`. - It holds `raw["implementation_pr"]` only when `kind == "issue"`, the value is an `int` (not a `bool`), it is `>= 1` and it is `!= item`. - Otherwise it is `None`. A malformed value is dropped, which fails closed to today's path. - Update the module docstring's context field list. **New helper `_existing_pr_route_ops(ctx, text) -> list[dict]`.** It returns `[]` unless all of these hold: `ctx["kind"] == "issue"`, `ctx["stop"] in EXISTING_PR_ROUTED_STOPS`, `ctx["implementation_pr"]` is set, and `_existing_pr_routing_enabled()`. When they hold, it returns these ops in order: 1. `{"op": "comment", "issue": pr, "body": f"Unblock judge instructions for #{item} (stop `{stop}`): {text}"}`. The fixed prefix means the comment can never start with a slash command. 2. `{"op": "dispatch_review", "pr": pr}` 3. `{"op": "remove_label", "issue": item, "label": present}`, only when the stop label is on the issue. **`reset_ops()` (L837).** In the issue branch, right after `present = ...` and before the `GUARD_STOPS` / `blocked` / `needs-human` branches, add: ``` routed = _existing_pr_route_ops(ctx, text) if routed: return routed ``` This is the only change to `reset_ops()`. With the flag off or no PR, the code falls through to today's lines unchanged. Because the check sits in `reset_ops`, it covers every caller: `plan()` `retry_budget`, `followup`, `hold-followup` and `regrant_ops`. `override_guard` calls `_approve` directly and is left unchanged; see D4. **New pure function and subcommand.** `implementation_pr_candidate(raw, item, repo, pipeline_login) -> {"pr": int|None, "reason": str}`, exposed as `impl-pr --graphql-file PATH --item N --repo R --pipeline-login L`. It is wired in `build_parser()` / `run()` the same way as `ci-owner`, and reads the GraphQL response described in section 2. - **Rule 1 (head branch):** among `repository.pullRequests` nodes, those with `headRepository.nameWithOwner` equal to `repo` (case-insensitive), the highest number wins. Reason: `head_branch`. - **Rule 2 (closes the issue):** among `CrossReferencedEvent.source` PRs, keep those that meet all of these: - `state == "OPEN"` - same-repository head - `author.login == pipeline_login` or `authorAssociation` in OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR - a body that matches the closing-keyword regex for `#N`, `owner/repo#N` or `https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/N`. This mirrors `closing_kw_re` in `.github/workflows/implement.yml`'s "Safety check for existing PR" step. Exactly one distinct match gives reason `closes`. More than one gives `pr: null, reason: ambiguous`. - Otherwise the result is `none`. A malformed payload gives `unreadable`. ### 2. `scripts/unblock_judge.sh` **New `unblock_existing_pr_routing_enabled()`.** It uses the same parsing as the flag reader in section 1 and defaults to `${UNBLOCK_EXISTING_PR_ROUTING_ENABLED:-true}`. An invalid value logs `UNBLOCK_JUDGE item= op=impl_pr outcome=disabled reason=invalid_flag`. **New `unblock_resolve_implementation_pr()`.** It follows the `unblock_resolve_ci_owner` pattern (L1736): it merges a key into `${RUNTIME_DIR}/context.json` and lets Python decide. - **When it runs:** only when `ITEM_KIND=issue`, `ITEM_STOP` is one of `needs-human|blocked|scope-blocked|destructive-blocked|implement-diagnose-failed`, and the flag is on. - **The read:** one `gh_retry gh api graphql` call that returns both `repository.pullRequests(headRefName:"ai/issue-", states:OPEN, first:5){number headRepository{nameWithOwner}}` and `repository.issue(number:N).timelineItems(itemTypes:[CROSS_REFERENCED_EVENT], last:50){... on CrossReferencedEvent{source{... on PullRequest{number state body headRepository{nameWithOwner} author{login} authorAssociation}}}}`. - **Parsing:** the response goes to `unblock_actions.py impl-pr --pipeline-login "${UNBLOCK_LOGIN}"`. When it returns a number, `jq '. + {implementation_pr: $n}'` merges it into `context.json`. - **Logging:** `UNBLOCK_JUDGE item= op=impl_pr outcome=found|none|unavailable pr= reason=`. - **Failure handling (fail open):** a failed read or parse leaves `context.json` unchanged, so today's behaviour runs. - **§14 audit comment:** for `ITEM_KIND=issue`, the earlier calls are the issue GET, the comments page and the run-metadata reads. None of them returns PRs. The only PR read (`pulls/${ITEM}`, around L1936) runs for `ITEM_KIND=pr` only. **Call site.** Call it once, directly after `context.json` is written (around L2021). Every later `unblock_actions.py` call (`plan`, `followup`, `hold-followup`, `regrant`) reads that file, so this covers all of them. **Header comment.** Document the flag (default true) in the env-var block near L46–80. **Op runner.** `unblock_run_ops` needs no change. Its `comment` op posts to `issues//comments`, which also works for a PR. Its `dispatch_review` op (L1442) already picks `ai-review.yml` or `internal-review.yml`. ### 3. `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` **Flag reader.** Add `UNBLOCK_EXISTING_PR_ROUTING_ENABLED="${UNBLOCK_EXISTING_PR_ROUTING_ENABLED:-true}"` next to `ENABLE_STALL_MERGED_PR_GUARD` (L3202), plus `_existing_pr_routing_enabled()` with the same on/off/warn rule (`::warning::` for an invalid value). **New helper `_stall_route_open_impl_pr `.** It runs only when the flag is on and returns: | rc | Case | Action | Logged line | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | Flag off, no open implementation PR, or `_resolve_issue_implementation_pr` failed or was inconclusive | Caller keeps today's `/approved` (fail open) | — | | 0 | Open PR found and `_dispatch_review_for_conflicts` returned 0 | Healing note added, `STALL_HEALING_CHANGED=true` | `STALL_RECOVERY issue= reason=open_impl_pr pr=

phase= action=dispatch_review override_from=` | | 2 | A review run is already active | None | `STALL_SKIP issue= reason=open_impl_pr_review_active pr=

phase= action=` | | 3 | The dispatch failed | None | `STALL_SKIP ... reason=open_impl_pr_dispatch_failed ...` | - **Finding the PR:** it reuses `_resolve_issue_implementation_pr` (L24105). It checks `STALL_IMPL_PR_JSON | .state == "open"` and takes the head ref from `.head.ref`. - **Dispatching review:** it reuses `_dispatch_review_for_conflicts` (L28556), which dispatches from the default branch only (#4701). **Call sites in `execute_stall_recovery_action`.** - `auto_approve` arm (around L20659): call the helper right after the no-op-cap block and before the staged-support / plan gates. - rc 0: set `STALL_RECOVERY_SHOULD_INCREMENT="true"` and `STALL_RECOVERY_EFFECTIVE_ACTION="dispatch_review"`, then `return 0`. - rc 2 or 3: `return 1`, with no increment. - rc 1: continue to today's code. - `retrigger_implement` arm (around L20722): the same call, after its no-op-cap block.
